subject: math

objective.text: Name numbers within 1 million. Use the place value chart and commas to group units.

explanations.title: Pattern of base ten units
explanations.text: Place values repeat in groups of three: ones, tens, hundreds. Then thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. Then millions, ten millions, hundred millions.

explanations.title: Naming bigger units
explanations.text: 10 hundred millions is renamed 1 billion. The next units are ten billions and hundred billions.

explanations.title: Commas group units by three
explanations.text: A comma marks each group of 3 digits. For example, ten billion is written 10,000,000,000.

explanations.title: Read a number by its groups
explanations.text: Read the number in each group. Then say the unit name of the group. 430,325 is read four hundred thirty thousand, three hundred twenty-five.

explanations.title: Bundle to the largest unit
explanations.text: Bundle 10 of one unit into 1 of the next larger unit.

explanations.title: 10 times with two units
explanations.text: Multiply each unit by 10. 10 times 5 hundreds 3 tens is 5 thousands 3 hundreds, or 5,300.

examples.title: Naming 608,430,325
examples.text: 608 millions, 430 thousands and 325 ones. Say it: six hundred eight million, four hundred thirty thousand, three hundred twenty-five.

examples.title: 2 groups of 5 hundreds
examples.text: 2 groups of 5 hundreds is 10 hundreds. Bundle them into 1 thousand.

examples.title: 10 times 15,309
examples.text: 10 × 15,309 = 153,090. Here 15,309 is 1 ten thousand 5 thousands 3 hundreds 9 ones.

hints.text: Think of the multiplication fact with the same numbers. Count by threes.
Count the places from the right. Say ones, tens, hundreds, then thousands.
Multiply the digit by its place value.
Think of the number of tens. Say it as a multiplication with 10.
Multiply by 10. Each unit moves one place left.
The names repeat in groups of three. Follow the pattern of thousands.
Add the units. If you have 10 of one unit, bundle them into the next larger unit.
Start at the right. Put a comma after each group of 3 digits.
Read each group of three digits. Then say the unit name of that group.
The thousands are the digits in front of the last three digits.
Turn each unit into standard form first. Then add the parts.
Multiply both units by 10. Then write the number in standard form.
Change both amounts to the same unit. Then compare.
